facts: The paper 'Why is AI-generated language so hard to understand?' was written by Thomas Hikaru Clark, Matias B. Martin, and Kyle Mahowald, and posted to arXiv on October 21, 2026 (id: arxiv:2610.29162).
The authors examine psycholinguistic features that correlate with human processing difficulty, including object relative clauses, long syntactic dependencies, and low-frequency n-grams.
The study compares text from a novel cross-domain corpus of AI-generated language against round-trip translation paraphrases and human writing.
All nine frontier and near-frontier AI models evaluated use more inanimate subjects with animate verbs and more low-frequency n-grams than human writing.
Most of the nine models also exhibit longer syntactic dependencies, more stacked nouns, and more reduced object relatives in conversational settings, with substantial variation across model families.
The paper hypothesizes that while human language optimizes for successful communication, AI text optimizes for information density driven by objectives like math, code, and reasoning.
The authors demonstrated proof-of-concept for their hypothesis by fine-tuning a language model under a length penalty, which induced divergence from human-like linguistic patterns.
